label: Brisnik HR-D2
title: Anticholinergic antidepressant after delirium, with another delirium-causing medicine
statement: Prescribed anticholinergic antidepressant opipramol, other TCAs (in doses ≥ 50 mg/day), or paroxetine - and the patient has a history of delirium and co-prescribed ≥ 1 further drug known to induce delirium (e.g., benzodiazepines, opioids, antihistamines, diuretics)[c]

plain_summary: Opipramol or paroxetine at any dose, or another tricyclic antidepressant at 50 mg a day or more, can bring on confusion again in a person who has had delirium, and more so when another medicine that can cause delirium is also taken.

medicine_groups.name: Opipramol at any dose and other tricyclic antidepressants at 50 mg/day or more
medicine_groups.note: Opipramol is not sold in Australia, so it is listed by ingredient only. The source does not list which medicines are 'other TCAs', so this list is a working list for the pharmacist to check. Work out the daily dose as the strength times the number of tablets or capsules taken each day. Low-dose amitriptyline under 50 mg a day does not count.

medicine_groups.name: Paroxetine (any dose)
medicine_groups.note: Paroxetine counts at any dose. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

medicine_groups.name: Benzodiazepines
medicine_groups.note: An example group. The source gives benzodiazepines only as an example of medicines known to induce delirium.

medicine_groups.name: Opioids
medicine_groups.note: An example group. Targin is oxycodone with naloxone. Panadeine Forte and Codalgin Forte are codeine with paracetamol. Australian codeine medicines require a prescription. Count recorded supplies, including combinations.

medicine_groups.name: Sedating antihistamines
medicine_groups.note: An example group. Many of these are sold without a prescription and may not appear in a dispensing history. Match diphenhydramine only from its recorded ingredient or a product specifically identified as containing it.

medicine_groups.name: Diuretics
medicine_groups.note: An example group. Combination products count under the diuretic they hold: Karvezide (irbesartan with hydrochlorothiazide), Micardis Plus (telmisartan with hydrochlorothiazide), Atacand Plus (candesartan with hydrochlorothiazide), Moduretic (amiloride with hydrochlorothiazide) and Coversyl Plus (perindopril with indapamide).

needs_facts.meets: A recorded episode of delirium before or during the period of combined prescribing.

options.words: Delirium before or during combined treatment
No delirium had occurred by the end of combined treatment

rule_for_models: Look for opipramol or Group B paroxetine at any dose, or another Group A tricyclic at 50 mg/day or more from strength and directions, plus a different delirium-inducing medicine such as those in Groups C to F, with overlapping supplies or dates within 60 days. Cite the supplies and a history of delirium by the time of combined prescribing, even if an earlier note denied it. With this medicine pair, report no finding if no delirium had yet occurred or the tricyclic dose was below its threshold. If the relevant history, timing or dose is unclear, report a possible finding, cite the supplies and available evidence, and ask for the missing information.
cannot_be_seen: Whether the person has ever had delirium, unless a line in the record says so. Which other medicines the person takes from other pharmacies or buys over the counter, and whether the other medicine is really taken.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether the antidepressant and the other delirium-causing medicine are both still needed, and, where the record is silent, a check of whether the person has had delirium before.
